content.title: About
content.content: Cheese sauce is a thick, flavorful sauce made from processed cheese, milk, and seasonings. It is commonly used as a topping for french fries, chicken nuggets, vegetables, and pasta dishes. The taste combines the creamy richness of cheese with a mild tang and aromatic spices.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cheese sauce originated in the United States in the mid‑20th century as a quick way to add a cheesy flavor to fast‑food items.
Emulsifiers such as mono‑ and diglycerides are often added to achieve a smooth texture.
There are many variations, including versions with chili, garlic, smoked cheese, or herbs.
In fast‑food restaurants the sauce is frequently served in small plastic packets.
In some countries the sauce is classified as a ready‑to‑heat product.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Cheese sauce provides calcium, which is essential for bone and teeth health.

items.title: Contains protein
items.content: It supplies a modest amount of protein that supports tissue repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The sauce contains vitamins B2 and B12, which help with energy metabolism.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: Fats aid the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins and contribute to satiety.

items.title: Enhances palatability
items.content: Cheese sauce makes foods more appealing, which can encourage a more varied diet.

items.title: High in fat and calories
items.content: Cheese sauce is calorie‑dense and contains saturated fats, so it should be consumed in moderation.

items.title: Lactose
items.content: It contains lactose, which may cause discomfort for those with intolerance.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: People allergic to milk or cheese may experience reactions.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: The sauce can be high in sodium, which is a concern for individuals with hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve cheese sauce warm with french fries, chicken nuggets, vegetable sticks, over pasta, in burritos, or as a base for casseroles. Heat it in the microwave or on the stovetop, stirring constantly.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the sauce refrigerated at 2 °C–5 °C. After opening, use within 5‑7 days. Do not freeze, as the texture may change.
